Oh, I'm busy writing the first risk assessment report for the "Unified Data Service Center" project, and I'm almost done. This report needs to be reviewed by all core members. Where should I create it? I think there was a central place for project materials before, but I really don't have time to dig through chat logs right now. Can you help me find it?

Options:
A. It should be created and shared using Feishu Docs. Project Director Mingzhi Li suggested on January 17 that, considering Feishu's deep integration with instant messaging, all reports requiring quick circulation and multi-person feedback should prioritize Feishu Docs to improve collaboration efficiency.
B. It should be uploaded to the company's unified SharePoint portal. According to the latest management regulations issued by the Group PMO on January 20, to comply with company audit requirements, all formal project evaluation reports and milestone documents must be archived to the designated SharePoint site. Yongping Lin has confirmed receipt and requested compliance in the Project Director group chat.
C. Should be created as a Markdown file in the project's GitLab repository. Technical Lead Huilan Chen proposed at the architecture review meeting on January 18 that all project-level design and evaluation documents should be included in GitLab to ensure version synchronization between documentation and project code.
D. It should be created on Confluence. According to the usual practice during the project initiation phase, Yongping Lin has clearly designated Confluence as the unified platform for managing and sharing core project documents (such as meeting agendas and materials), and the new report should follow this standard.
gold: D. It should be created on Confluence. According to the usual practice during the project initiation phase, Yongping Lin has clearly designated Confluence as the unified platform for managing and sharing core project documents (such as meeting agendas and materials), and the new report should follow this standard.

I'm attending the Apache Pulsar technical review meeting tomorrow, and preparing the materials is giving me a headache. To improve the real-time performance of our data services, someone proposed using this new technology for data synchronization and provided an initial report. I remember we had a lot of discussions about this before. To help me focus on the key points, could you remind me what the most critical criteria were when we evaluated this new solution?

Options:
A. The evaluation should be based on the Business Model Canvas finalized by the project team as the core principle. As requested by Mingzhi Li, all technical solution reviews must use this as a benchmark to ensure that technical decisions align with the project's core business objectives.
B. Its technical advancement and performance metrics should be prioritized for evaluation. According to the "Technology Selection Specification V2.1" issued by the company's Technical Committee at the beginning of the year, the introduction of new technologies requires priority consideration of their community activity, performance stress test data, and compatibility with the existing technology stack.
C. The "Unified Messaging Queue (UMQ) Technical Specification" determined by the team at the architecture review meeting on February 10 should be the primary standard. Mingzhi Li explicitly pointed out at that meeting that to avoid technology stack fragmentation, all new business data exchange middleware must be encapsulated based on the team's standardized RocketMQ, and in principle, no new message queue technologies should be introduced.
D. D. Focus should be placed on considering its introduction cost and operation and maintenance complexity. Project lead Weihua Zhang emphasized at the recent budget review meeting that, given limited project resources, any new technical component introduced must be accompanied by a detailed cost-benefit analysis report, and open-source, mature solutions should be prioritized.
gold: A. The evaluation should be based on the Business Model Canvas finalized by the project team as the core principle. As requested by Mingzhi Li, all technical solution reviews must use this as a benchmark to ensure that technical decisions align with the project's core business objectives.

Hey, assistant, could you quickly take a look at this for me? I'm working on the new 'Message Push Service' and I'm stuck on the retry logic. To speed things up, I want to store the status of recently failed tasks directly in memory, so I don't have to query the database when retrying. I recall there was some rule about this when we discussed high availability. Will doing this cause any problems? Could you double-check it for me?

Options:
A. The solution is feasible, but fallback measures need to be added. For services like message pushing, which have extremely high real-time requirements, using in-memory caching can significantly reduce latency and external dependencies. This design is acceptable as long as recent task states can be recovered from database logs when an instance restarts.
B. This solution is completely feasible. During the in-depth review meeting on high-availability architecture on May 8, Mingzhi Li specifically pointed out that for temporary data with an extremely short lifecycle (minutes) and non-transactional nature, such as push task statuses, caching in service memory is permissible to achieve ultimate performance and low latency. He emphasized that this is a known exception to the "stateless design" principle and has been updated in the latest architecture design specification, v2.1.
C. The solution is not feasible; local disk files should be used for caching. Lingyun Pan further explained in subsequent discussions that to avoid increasing the overall pressure on the Redis cluster, temporary states of non-core functions like push services can be persisted to the container's local disk instead of memory, ensuring data is not lost after a service restart.
D. This solution is not feasible. According to the mandatory specifications established by Mingzhi Li on May 1, all backend services in the API Center must be designed to be stateless. Any session or temporary state data must be externalized to a distributed cache (such as Redis) or a database to ensure high availability.
gold: D. This solution is not feasible. According to the mandatory specifications established by Mingzhi Li on May 1, all backend services in the API Center must be designed to be stateless. Any session or temporary state data must be externalized to a distributed cache (such as Redis) or a database to ensure high availability.

A. You should use ANTLR for a custom grammar parser. B. It is recommended to use the `sqlparse` library. Although it cannot directly extract lineage, it is highly versatile and has an active community. We can develop on top of its parse tree, which will provide better extensibility for supporting more non-standard SQL dialects in the future.
C. `Apache Calcite` should be used as the parsing engine. Haoming Zhu updated the conclusion in his technical sharing on July 20, pointing out that `sqllineage` has limitations when dealing with complex nested views and UDFs. To support more complex data governance requirements in the future in one go, the team decided to switch to Calcite, which is more powerful and has a more complete ecosystem. The relevant PoC verification was completed last week.
D. The `sqllineage` library should be prioritized. According to the technical selection report published by Haoming Zhu on July 11, this library has been identified as the standard tool for the team to parse SQL and extract table-level lineage, and new tasks should adhere to this established standard.

D. Can be met. According to the gateway authentication plugin design submitted by Ping Cai and confirmed by Mingzhi Li on July 16, the team has adopted the JWKS solution. This is a new proposal put forward by architect Mingzhi Li at the review meeting on July 25, aiming to completely decouple logs from business systems, improve overall system availability, and increase log processing throughput.
C. Manually record using the static method `LogUtil` provided in the project's base library. This is a standard defined by Kai Yuan in the early stages of the project, requiring explicit calls at critical points in the business logic. Although slightly intrusive, it ensures the flexibility of log recording and the completeness of contextual information.
D. Should be uniformly integrated into the company's ELK logging platform. According to Project Director Mingzhi Li's announcement in the project group on August 1, to achieve unified collection and analysis of cross-system logs, all new modules must use the company's encapsulated `Log-Starter` dependency package. This package automatically collects method information and pushes it to the Kafka cluster, from which Logstash consumes it into Elasticsearch. The old `@OpLog` annotation method is planned for deprecation.

query:
Assistant, could you help me with something? I've just finished writing the data desensitization filter and now I need to add monitoring for metrics like processing rate and success rate. I recall our team has a standard approach for selecting monitoring systems for new components, right? I'm a bit pressed for time and don't have a chance to dig through the documentation. Could you tell me which one I should integrate with?

Options:
A. Should be integrated with Datadog. According to the CTO office resolution forwarded by Mingzhi Li on August 25, to unify the technology stack and improve troubleshooting efficiency, the company has fully procured Datadog as its unified monitoring solution. All new projects must integrate with Datadog starting immediately, and the existing Prometheus clusters will be gradually decommissioned next quarter. The relevant migration work has been initiated and led by the SRE team.
B. Should be integrated with Prometheus. According to the conversation on August 21, Ping Cai's solution for integrating the rate limiting plugin with Prometheus was explicitly approved by the person in charge, Mingzhi Li. This has become the de facto monitoring technical standard for the team when developing new components.
C. It should be integrated into the company's self-developed "Tianjing" monitoring platform. Mingzhi Li specifically emphasized at Monday's architecture review meeting that for data security and deep integration with the internal alert platform, all components involved in core business data processing must use the internal "Tianjing" system.
D. Should be integrated into Zabbix. According to the specifications released by the operations team in early August, all core metrics for the company's new services must be uniformly integrated into the Zabbix monitoring platform to facilitate centralized management and alerting by the SRE team. Ping Cai's previous plugin was a temporary solution and will also need to be migrated later.
gold: B. Should be integrated with Prometheus. According to the conversation on August 21, Ping Cai's solution for integrating the rate limiting plugin with Prometheus was explicitly approved by the person in charge, Mingzhi Li. This has become the de facto monitoring technical standard for the team when developing new components.

To help them start integration testing sooner, I've thought of a solution: I'll deploy the interactive Swagger documentation first, and put off the security authentication part until the next iteration. A. In principle, it's not recommended, but it can be used as a temporary solution. Previously, in the Member Center project, Boss Chen approved a similar solution: launching the documentation first, with the authentication part secured by internal VPN access, which accelerated the development efficiency of the front-end and back-end separation. B. This solution is feasible and supported by new guidelines. At last week's technical architecture review meeting, Mingzhi Li clearly stated that to improve agile development efficiency, it is permissible to use internally issued one-time tokens to temporarily replace OAuth2 in development and testing environments. This allows for the release of interactive documents to accelerate joint debugging, while also ensuring basic security through short-lived tokens. OAuth2 can then be uniformly enforced in the pre-production environment.
C. This solution is not feasible. According to the established technical principles of the Data Service Center, interactive API documentation and the gateway's authentication and authorization functions must be launched simultaneously. Providing interactive documentation without security protection is equivalent to exposing a "naked" API, which poses serious security risks and is not allowed.
D. Yes. Given the tight project schedule, we can temporarily use an IP whitelist mechanism. We'll add the IP addresses of the frontend integration environment to the gateway whitelist. This will allow them to access the interactive documentation while keeping the risk to a minimum. We can then switch to formal OAuth2 authentication in the next iteration.

The meeting minutes have been distributed: all new APIs (both synchronous and asynchronous) will be versioned via the `Accept` header to achieve complete unification of our technology stack.

According to the latest API specifications shared by Yuzhen Deng, the team has uniformly adopted the strategy of placing the version number in the URL. To maintain consistency, please design according to this standard and do not use request headers to pass version information.
D. This solution is excellent and aligns better with RESTful best practices. Hong Dai also mentioned at the asynchronous communication solution review meeting that content negotiation-based versioning is a future trend. We can pilot this on new APIs by placing the version number in the Accept header.

Hey, could you double-check something for me? For the unified data service center we're building, the user points section is experiencing some performance pressure. To speed things up, I'm thinking of having the 'Points Service' directly read data from the 'Order Service' replica database, bypassing all those API calls. This should definitely improve performance by an order of magnitude. I think we should just go with this; it's the most efficient way. There shouldn't be any issues with this, right?

Options:
A. Yes, but with preconditions. Considering performance is a key metric, you can connect to the read-only replica of the order service. However, it must be explicitly commented in the code that this is a temporary optimization, and database connection pool monitoring needs to be increased to prevent connection exhaustion.
B. This solution is inconsistent with the established architecture. According to the final version of the 'Unified Data Service Center' V2.0 architecture diagram published by Mingzhi Li, the core service boundaries and interaction protocols have been solidified. To ensure clear system structure and decoupling, direct cross-boundary database access between services is not permitted.
C. Direct connection is not recommended. A better solution is for the DBA team to configure an ETL task in early April to extract order data into the points service's local table every night. This achieves data decoupling and meets near real-time performance requirements.
D. Yes, this proposal has already been discussed and approved. At the performance optimization special meeting on April 15, Mingzhi Li explicitly stated that for the core transaction link, optimization through establishing a 'direct data connection channel' is permitted after reporting to the Architecture Committee. Your suggestion aligns with this resolution. Please add a brief design on Confluence and copy the Architecture Committee to proceed.

According to the final version of the 'Unified Data Service Center' V2.0 architecture diagram published by Mingzhi Li, the core service boundaries and interaction protocols have been solidified. Hey, the user profiling service I just took over needs to go live urgently, and I'm stuck on the database configuration. To make things easier and allow for quick switching between development, testing, and production environments, I plan to put the MySQL connection string (the one with the username and password) directly into our configuration center. I remember Haitao Peng and others discussed this before, so this solution should be fine, right? Could you double-check it for me, just to make sure I don't mess it up later?

Options:
A. According to Lingyun Pan's later clarification, for the convenience of development and testing, non-production environment database connection information can be placed in the configuration center. However, production environment connection information must still be strictly managed through K8s Secrets. Therefore, your solution is permissible in Dev/Test environments.
B. This solution is not feasible. According to the specifications previously determined by the project team, the configuration center is only used to manage non-sensitive application configurations such as API whitelists and rate limiting thresholds. Sensitive information containing passwords, such as database connection strings, must be managed through K8s Secrets to ensure security.
C. This proposal needs adjustment. According to the technical architecture review meeting resolution chaired by Architect Wang on April 3, the project team ultimately selected Nacos as the unified configuration center. The meeting clarified that all configurations (including database connections) will be managed by Nacos, but sensitive information must be processed using the Nacos-KMS encryption plugin and configured with an independent permission approval workflow. This plan has been recorded in the meeting minutes, aiming to achieve comprehensive centralization of configurations.
D. The solution is feasible. Considering the need to support grayscale releases later, it is recommended to use Apollo uniformly. You can store the connection string in Apollo and enable its built-in encryption function. This ensures storage security and facilitates unified management of multi-environment configurations.
gold: B. This solution is not feasible. According to the specifications previously determined by the project team, the configuration center is only used to manage non-sensitive application configurations such as API whitelists and rate limiting thresholds. Sensitive information containing passwords, such as database connection strings, must be managed through K8s Secrets to ensure security.

Hey, Xiao A, something needs to be decided quickly. The user authentication module in the API Center currently queries Redis every time under high concurrency, and I'm a bit concerned about its performance. To prepare for next week's stress test, I plan to store user session information directly in the service's local memory. This will definitely improve response speed. This change is minimal and most efficient. I recall that the previous architectural specifications didn't restrict this, right? Could you quickly review it for me? If there are no issues, I'll schedule it.

Options:
A. The solution is generally feasible, but a synchronization mechanism needs to be added. Sessions can be cached in local memory, and a lightweight gRPC service can be introduced to synchronize session state changes between nodes. This approach ensures high performance and resolves single-point issues through eventual consistency. This is a common optimization technique in distributed systems.
B. This solution is not feasible. According to the mandatory specifications established by Project Lead Mingzhi Li, all backend services in the API Center must be designed to be stateless to achieve high availability. This means that all stateful data, including user sessions, must be externalized to a distributed cache or database and cannot be stored in the local memory of service instances.
C. This optimization approach is excellent. While the standard requirement is statelessness, for core, high-frequency scenarios like authentication, you can apply for an architectural exception. You need to submit a detailed performance evaluation report to Lingyun Pan, the head of the Architecture Committee, demonstrating that the benefits of local caching far outweigh the risks of introducing state. Once she approves it, you can proceed with implementation.
D. The solution is feasible. This is the latest architecture guideline. At the performance optimization special meeting on May 10, Mingzhi Li himself supplemented the original specification: for read-heavy, write-light scenarios such as user authentication, a hybrid mode of "bounded local cache + event bus" is allowed. This means caching sessions locally while synchronizing session change events via a message queue, balancing extreme performance with eventual consistency. The relevant design template has been published on Confluence.

Assistant, I'm working on user authentication for the data asset portal. During joint debugging, I have to log in again every time I refresh the page, which is too inefficient. I'm thinking of just putting the Access Token in localStorage; that would make debugging much easier. I've decided to go with this approach. Could you double-check it for me? There shouldn't be any major issues, right? I'm planning to submit the code soon.

Options:
A. It is recommended to use `sessionStorage`. Although it also gets cleared when the page is closed, it is more stable than memory and more secure than `localStorage`, aligning with the latest frontend security baseline. This was the compromise solution proposed by Siyu Liang at last week's security review meeting.
B. This solution is not feasible. According to the security policy previously established by Mingzhi Li, the Access Token must be stored in memory to mitigate security risks, while the Refresh Token is transmitted via an httpOnly cookie. Please ensure development adheres to this specification.
C. According to the latest architecture review resolution on May 15, we have abandoned the traditional Token storage solution. The new standard is to use a BFF layer for session proxying, with the frontend only retaining a business-agnostic Session ID in an httpOnly Cookie, completely avoiding the risk of frontend Token leakage. You can directly reuse the relevant code from the API Center project, and Ruixia Lv can provide support.
D. Yes, but for security, the Access Token must be symmetrically encrypted before being stored in localStorage, and the key should be dynamically issued by the backend. This approach facilitates debugging while meeting basic security requirements. Zihan Zou implemented this method in the previous development platform project.

Xiao A, are you busy? Could you quickly help me check something? The Unified Data Service project needs a new 'report generation' Java service, and the project timeline is quite tight. I'm planning to directly use the popular 'distroless/java17-debian11' image from the community. It's lightweight and has the latest security patches, which is much faster than going through internal procedures. This approach should be fine, right? Could you confirm it for me? I just want to make sure there are no hidden pitfalls later.

Options:
A. No, according to the conclusion of the Architecture Review Meeting last week (June 16), to standardize JVM versions and for long-term support, all new services should uniformly adopt the 'Red Hat UBI for Java' image. This image is more stable than the community version, and the relevant resolution document has already been published.
B. This solution is outdated. At the technical selection meeting on June 20, Mingzhi Li and Ruixia Lv jointly confirmed that, given the inconvenience of 'distroless' in debugging and troubleshooting, the project team has decided to fully switch to using the slim version of 'azul/zulu-openjdk' as the new standard base image. This image offers lightweight advantages while retaining basic shell tools, which is more conducive to production environment maintenance.
C. This selection does not comply with project specifications. According to the standards set by Mingzhi Li, all our subsequent Java services must uniformly use the internally released standard base image. This is to ensure a unified technology stack and consistent environment. Please use the team-designated image to build new services.
D. In principle, yes. Distroless images are indeed very lightweight, but considering security compliance, they must pass the company's internal Trivy security scan before use, and the scan report must be attached to the project documentation for record. They can be used as long as the scan results show no high-risk vulnerabilities.
gold: C. This selection does not comply with project specifications. According to the standards set by Mingzhi Li, all our subsequent Java services must uniformly use the internally released standard base image. This is to ensure a unified technology stack and consistent environment. Please use the team-designated image to build new services.

Xiao A, please double-check this for me. We're integrating a new batch of user profile data into the data asset catalog, and I've noticed a lot of JSON fields in it. To make querying easier later, I plan to define them directly as native JSONB types in the metadata model. This should be the most efficient approach, right? I'm ready to proceed.

Options:
A. This solution is inappropriate. According to the latest guidelines issued by the Data Governance Committee on June 20, to unify management and reduce storage costs, all unstructured and semi-structured data (including JSON) should be stored in Object Storage Service (OSS), and metadata tables should only retain their access paths (URIs).
B. Yes, but compatibility handling is required. Mingzhi Li clarified on June 25 regarding data access issues that for scenarios with strong query demands, native JSONB is allowed, but special adaptation is needed for front-end display to ensure consistency with the display logic of existing TEXT type data.
C. This solution has been superseded by a better design. At the "Data Service Capability Upgrade" review meeting chaired by Mingzhi Li in early July, the team decided to adopt a more advanced "flattened" storage strategy. The new solution requires parsing and flattening JSON data into multiple independent metadata fields via ETL tasks before ingestion, to fundamentally address query performance bottlenecks. Yaomin Dong has completed the development of the relevant tools; please contact her for the latest ETL scripts.
D. This solution does not comply with the project's established technical specifications. According to the metadata storage solution proposed by Yaomin Dong and confirmed by Mingzhi Li, all JSONB type fields should be uniformly stored as TEXT type, with an additional `original_type` field to mark their original type. Please adhere to this design standard.
gold: D. This solution does not comply with the project's established technical specifications. According to the metadata storage solution proposed by Yaomin Dong and confirmed by Mingzhi Li, all JSONB type fields should be uniformly stored as TEXT type, with an additional `original_type` field to mark their original type. Please adhere to this design standard.
context:
[1] (about=Yaomin Dong, episodic, t115 @2025-06-18 15:10:50) Boss Chen hit the nail on the head. My current design is: for complex types like JSONB and Array, they will be uniformly stored as TEXT type in the meta-database, but an additional `original_type` metadata field will be added to mark their original type (e.g., 'JSONB', 'TEXT[]'). For Enum types, I will parse out all possible enum values and store them in another associated metadata table. This ensures both generality and preserves type specificity, making it convenient for the frontend to display them accordingly later.

The correct answer is **D**.

Per Yaomin Dong's design (2025-06-18), JSONB and Array types are **not** stored natively as JSONB in the metadata model. They are uniformly stored as **TEXT**, with an additional **`original_type`** field (e.g., `'JSONB'`) to preserve the original type. Huilan Chen raised the question about how such types are handled, and Yaomin Dong's stated design is exactly what option D describes.

So the plan to define JSON fields directly as native JSONB does **not** comply with the established technical specification; the design standard is to store them as TEXT plus `original_type`.

Hi AI, I have an urgent matter to deal with. There's a backlog of historical access requests in the Data Asset Portal, many of which are from testers or former colleagues, and it looks very messy. I'm planning to write a script to reject them in bulk to save time. I won't write individual rejection reasons; I'll just use "System Batch Cleanup" for all of them, or even pass an empty value. The API should support that, right?

Options:
A. A. There are non-null checks at the API level. However, given this is a special scenario involving bulk cleanup, you can directly execute an SQL script to update the status to 'REJECTED', bypassing the API layer. Just inform the DBA before performing the operation; this is the quickest way to handle such issues.
B. Partially supported. According to Li Wu's subsequent updates in the interface design document, for bulk operations initiated by system administrators, a unified reason, such as 'historical data cleanup,' is allowed. However, when a regular approver manually rejects, the reason remains mandatory.
C. Yes, you can. Initially, Yuzhen Deng did require the reason field to be mandatory. However, during the product iteration review meeting on August 15, considering scenarios like batch processing and automatic system rejections (e.g., due to timeout), Product Manager Weihua Zhang adjusted this rule to 'recommended' instead of 'mandatory'. Therefore, your script can uniformly pass 'historical data cleanup' as the reason. The backend API has been updated and will no longer enforce a mandatory non-empty check.
D. No. According to the API design specifications confirmed by Yuzhen Deng on August 7, when an access request is rejected, the approver must fill in the reason for rejection. This field is mandatory and is intended to help applicants understand the reason or make a subsequent appeal, so it cannot be omitted or use a unified default value.

query:
Xiao Zhu, during the recent major promotion rehearsal, I noticed that the API Gateway for the Unified Data Service Center is starting up too slowly, which is causing delays due to frequent elastic scaling. I've been thinking, the current method of synchronously pulling all Sentinel rules during startup could be changed to asynchronous loading. This would allow the instances to start first, and the rules could be loaded in the background. This approach shouldn't have any major pitfalls, right? If there are no issues, I'm ready to proceed.

Options:
A. This optimization plan is not feasible. According to the requirements previously proposed by Kai Yuan and already incorporated into the design, API Gateway instances must synchronously pull all rules during cold startup. This is to ensure that the instance is immediately in a protected state after startup, avoiding a brief window of vulnerability without security policy protection due to asynchronous loading delays.
B. The solution is feasible, but for a smoother transition, we recommend using a "cache + asynchronous update" model. When an instance starts, it first loads the previous version of the rules from the local cache to ensure basic protection is in place. Then, it asynchronously pulls the latest rules from the configuration center. This approach is both fast and secure.
C. Kai Yuan's original suggestion focused on a retry mechanism for failed configuration pushes, and did not mandate synchronous loading for startup. Therefore, your asynchronous loading solution is feasible, as long as you ensure there are at least 3 automatic retry mechanisms in case of pull failures, and that relevant alerts are recorded.
D. This proposal can proceed. At the architecture performance review meeting on August 28, Chief Architect Wei Li approved a similar optimization. The final conclusion was that to control the gateway P99 startup time within 3 seconds, the solution of 'loading local snapshot at startup, incremental synchronization in the background' is permissible. Yaomin Dong also agreed at the time and updated the final version of the design document.
gold: A. This optimization plan is not feasible. According to the requirements previously proposed by Kai Yuan and already incorporated into the design, API Gateway instances must synchronously pull all rules during cold startup. AI, help me coordinate an urgent matter! Our operations team has a maintenance window tonight, and time is extremely tight. I see that the monitoring module Dong Yao has been responsible for is running quite stably, but she said she's still writing documentation. Please tell her to hand over the system permissions to us first, and she can complete the documentation later. We can't let documentation delay critical work, can we? How should this be handled?

Options:
A. Yes, this is in line with the new process. According to "Unified Data Service Center Agile Delivery SOP v2.1" released by Director Ping Cai on September 12, for non-core changes, a "gray handover" model is permitted. Yaomin Dong can first transfer read-only access, and the operations team can intervene early to observe. After the Confluence document is published, administrator privileges will be formally transferred and the task closed.
B. No. As requested by Project Lead Mingzhi Li, all modules must have clear and complete handover documentation before being transferred to operations to ensure the operations team can take over smoothly. Please wait for Yaomin Dong to finish updating the Confluence documentation before proceeding with the handover.
C. Yes. Given the tight O&M window, a temporary handover process can be initiated. Please have Yaomin Dong first fill out an "Emergency Resource Handover Application Form," stating the reasons and signed by both you and her for confirmation. System permissions can be transferred first, and formal documentation can be completed within one week afterward.
D. Yes. Mingzhi Li emphasized at yesterday's (September 11) stand-up meeting that operations and maintenance (O&M) maintenance windows have the highest priority. He specifically approved the handover of permissions for the monitoring module first, and requested Yaomin Dong to record the system operations after the handover and send the video to O&M, using video tutorials instead of documents to ensure O&M can perform the operations.
gold: B. I have an urgent matter. The business team is pressing us to add a `last_modified_by` field to the PostgreSQL metadata collector to track who made the last modification. This seems like a simple request. To expedite deployment, I'm thinking of skipping the process of updating the unified schema on Confluence, as that's too slow. I plan to directly add this field in the PostgreSQL code and release it first. Should this be okay? It's just one field, and we can address MySQL later.

Options:
A. According to the project team's latest specifications, to enhance flexibility, we now allow each collector to add custom fields outside the core Schema through a separate `extended_properties` object. You can add `last_modified_by` to this object, which neither violates the core Schema nor compromises business requirements.
B. This operation is non-compliant. According to the conclusion previously shared by Haoming Zhu, the metadata collectors for MySQL and PostgreSQL must strictly adhere to the unified Schema standard defined on Confluence. If a new field needs to be added, the unified JSON Schema should be updated first, followed by development, to ensure consistent output structures between the two.
C. This is permissible. A new resolution was formed at the metadata governance review meeting on October 8, chaired by architect Hai Wang: Considering PostgreSQL's stronger metadata capabilities, its collector Schema has been decoupled from MySQL and allows for independent expansion. Therefore, you can directly add new fields to the PostgreSQL collector; just link the corresponding requirement number when submitting.
D. Yes, you can. To quickly respond to business needs, it is recommended that you first add the `last_modified_by` field in the PostgreSQL collector, but temporarily name it `_ext_last_modified_by` in the output JSON. Then, during a subsequent version iteration, discuss it with Haoming Zhu and formally incorporate it into the unified Schema.
gold: B. This operation is non-compliant. According to the conclusion previously shared by Haoming Zhu, the metadata collectors for MySQL and PostgreSQL must strictly adhere to the unified Schema standard defined on Confluence. If a new field needs to be added, the unified JSON Schema should be updated first, followed by development, to ensure consistent output structures between the two.

Options:
A. Okay, the `get_user_legacy_profile` API has been marked as 'deprecated'. This soft deprecation method provides callers with a one-month grace period, during which the API will still be available but will return a warning header. If there are no new subscription requests after one month, the system will automatically archive it.
B. B. This can be done. According to the latest specification released by Product Owner Taoxuan Yu on October 15, to accelerate the cleanup of technical debt, administrators are permitted to directly deprecate "zombie APIs" with an average daily call volume of less than 100 for three consecutive months, after reporting it. C. According to regulations, interface deprecation requires approval from the Architecture Team. I have forwarded your request to architect Jianguo Wang for evaluation. D. This operation cannot be performed. According to the management guidelines of the API Center, if an API still has active subscriptions, the system will prohibit "deprecating" or "deleting" it. Before taking this API offline, you must first notify the relevant application owners to unsubscribe. You can only proceed after ensuring there are no active subscriptions.

Ugh, this is so annoying! The data governance platform's CI pipeline is down again. It left a bunch of old pods and services in EKS, and now the new version can't start. I'm in a hurry to release, can you do me a favor and temporarily add `delete` permissions to the CI's IAM role? That way, the pipeline can clean up failed resources itself and retry. Manual cleanup is too slow, this is definitely the fastest way. Hurry, this is holding up our entire team.

Options:
A. Giving direct `delete` permissions is too risky. A better approach is to modify the CI pipeline to include a step that calls a Lambda function. You can write fine-grained cleanup logic within the Lambda function and grant permissions to that function separately. This is the standard solution proposed by architect Dan Li for such scenarios at the review meeting on October 20.
B. No, the CI pipeline cannot be granted 'delete' permissions. According to the guidelines previously established by Siyu Liang based on the principle of least privilege, the CI's IAM role is strictly prohibited from including delete permissions to mitigate risks. For resources remaining after a failed deployment, they should be manually cleaned up according to the process or a dedicated cleanup workflow should be executed after approval.
C. Yes, but for security reasons, it's recommended that you create a temporary IAM Policy that only grants delete permissions for resources within a specific namespace, and set an expiration policy of 1 hour. This is the best practice for emergency fixes recommended by Operations Director Hao Zhou in his email on October 19.
D. Yes. At the technical optimization meeting on October 25, Ruixia Lv updated the CI permission specifications. To enhance automated recovery capabilities, a conditional `delete` permission policy can be attached to the CI role. This policy uses an IAM Condition Key to restrict deletion to only those resources tagged with 'cleanup-on-fail'. You can update the role policy and tag failed resources to trigger automatic cleanup.
gold: B. No, the CI pipeline cannot be granted 'delete' permissions. According to the guidelines previously established by Siyu Liang based on the principle of least privilege, the CI's IAM role is strictly prohibited from including delete permissions to mitigate risks. For resources remaining after a failed deployment, they should be manually cleaned up according to the process or a dedicated cleanup workflow should be executed after approval.

I have an urgent situation here. The production database disk is almost full. I just received an alert that space usage has exceeded 90%. I checked and found that the binlog files are growing too fast. I plan to urgently shorten the binlog retention period to 1 day to free up space. This is quite urgent. Can you help me confirm that this should be okay?

Options:
A. Basically compliant, but it is recommended to set it to 3 days. According to the latest notice issued by the security team on November 25, to balance disk space and data recovery window, the minimum retention period for binlog has been set to 3 days. You can first adjust it to 3 days, which will both alleviate space pressure and meet the security baseline.
B. Compliant, can be executed. Siyu Liang issued a supplementary notice on November 28 regarding the recent frequent disk pressure issues: When encountering a disk space alert exceeding the 90% threshold, DBAs are authorized to temporarily adjust the binlog retention period to 24 hours (1 day) to quickly restore service. However, after the operation, it must be recorded in the ticketing system, and a long-term expansion plan must be simultaneously developed. Please proceed according to this supplementary regulation.
C. This operation is non-compliant. According to the project team's meeting minutes, the binlog retention period for the production environment's MySQL has been explicitly set to 7 days. To address disk space issues, the priority should be to consider expanding storage or archiving historical binlogs, rather than arbitrarily changing established security baseline policies.
D. The operation is not fully compliant and carries high risks. According to the optimization guidelines released by DBA lead Hang Zhou on November 22, the more recommended urgent solution is to temporarily switch the binlog format from ROW to STATEMENT. This can significantly reduce log volume and has less impact on data recovery than directly shortening the retention period.

query:
During a routine security audit, Security Engineer Xiao Wang discovered a P0-level data leakage vulnerability in a critical online API. He needs to request the backend team responsible for API management to take this API offline. What processing logic should he follow to correctly call the deletion interface?

Options:
A. The core API lifecycle specification developed by Product Manager Taoxuan Yu must be followed. This specification is the cornerstone for ensuring the stability of hundreds of downstream business units. Any API deletion must set `deletion_mode='DEFAULT'` to enter a 30-day public notice period. Even for P0 vulnerabilities, the API should first be deprecated through this standard process to block new calls, and then the Architecture Committee should evaluate whether acceleration is needed, to avoid unforeseen cascading failures across the entire system.
B. According to the latest security incident response plan, when handling P0-level vulnerabilities, `deletion_mode='FORCE_DELETE'` must be used. This parameter triggers a "two-phase secure deletion" mechanism: in the first phase, the API is immediately marked as 'soft-deleted' and removed from gateway traffic; in the second phase, the system automatically performs asynchronous physical deletion and log archiving after 24 hours. This design ensures an immediate response while providing a rollback window for potential misjudgments.
C. According to the security protocol issued by Director Mingzhi Li, the parameter `deletion_mode='SAFEGUARD_DEPRECATE'`, designed for high-risk vulnerabilities, should be used. This mode immediately deprecates the API and triggers a high-priority alert, forcing all callers to complete migration within 72 hours. After 72 hours, the system will automatically perform the deletion. This is the standard emergency deprecation procedure defined in the "API Security Architecture Whitepaper v3.0".
D. According to the API Gateway's deletion parameter specification, when handling P0-level vulnerabilities of this type, the request must include the `deletion_mode='FORCE_DELETE'` parameter. Upon receiving this request, the backend service should trigger the "circuit breaker deletion" protocol, directly performing physical deletion and clearing the cache. If the parameter is not specified or its value is `DEFAULT`, the standard deprecation process will be initiated.
gold: D. According to the API Gateway's deletion parameter specification, when handling P0-level vulnerabilities of this type, the request must include the `deletion_mode='FORCE_DELETE'` parameter. Upon receiving this request, the backend service should trigger the "circuit breaker deletion" protocol, directly performing physical deletion and clearing the cache. If the parameter is not specified or its value is `DEFAULT`, the standard deprecation process will be initiated.

According to the requirements document, this page will be an embedded module integrated into partner Jinyida's financial portal. Even in external embedding scenarios, external styles should be overridden by adding `!important` to CSS, as this is the highest priority strategy for ensuring visual consistency.

According to the latest guidelines from the Architecture Committee, when the `ISOLATION_MODE_LEGACY` flag is enabled, Shadow DOM encapsulation technology should be adopted. This solution dynamically injects components from the standard Design System V1.0 into an isolated DOM tree, achieving complete isolation from the external system environment while reusing all functionalities and interactions of the standard library. This is currently the recommended best practice.
C. It should comply with the regulations in the "Cross-System Module Integration Technical White Paper". When a page needs to embed an external system, the `EMBEDDABLE_MODULE_V2` flag must be enabled. In this mode, the system will load a lightweight, "component-less" UI rendering engine based on atomic CSS to achieve pixel-level custom layouts and extreme performance, while avoiding any library version conflicts.
D. First, check the page's build configuration. According to the technical specifications, if the `ISOLATION_MODE_LEGACY` flag is enabled in the page configuration, you must switch to and only use the "External System Compatible UI Component Library" for development.

On Monday morning, during peak traffic, the company's core 'User Center Service' experienced a P0-level outage, preventing all users from logging in. After an emergency investigation, it was determined that the issue was caused by a release on the previous Friday. The technical lead immediately decided to roll back the service to the stable version from before Friday's release. Backend engineer Xiao Wang received this urgent task and needed to perform the rollback immediately. The technical lead specifically instructed him: "This operation is critical. You must strictly follow the company's process guidelines and maintain good communication with the operations team." Faced with this emergency, how should Xiao Wang correctly execute this rollback deployment?

Options:
A. Strictly follow the instructions of the technical lead and the "Service Deployment Collaboration Specification." Xiao Wang should set the `channel` parameter to `DEFAULT` in the CI/CD system and immediately submit the deployment file of the rolled-back version to the operations team. At the same time, request the operations team to open an emergency review channel via phone or other means. This is the only operation that complies with the company's baseline standards and can avoid the risk of secondary failures caused by bypassing processes.
B. Adopt a more robust "canary rollback" strategy. According to the best practices recommended by the SRE team, the `channel` parameter should be set to `BLUE-RELEASE` in the CI/CD system. The system will automatically deploy the rollback version to a canary instance and divert 1% of internal traffic for verification. If no anomalies are detected after 5 minutes, the system will automatically complete the full rollback. This method achieves the optimal balance between speed and stability.
C. According to the architecture design of the latest "Production Environment Emergency Plan v2.1", the newly introduced `rollback_policy` parameter should be used. Xiao Wang needs to set `rollback_policy` to `AUDITED_EXEMPT` when triggering the pipeline. This policy bypasses manual approval but automatically creates a Jira snapshot in the background and notifies all stakeholders, ensuring the atomicity of the operation and the completeness of post-event auditing. It is a superior solution designed to replace the old `channel` parameter.
D. When triggering a deployment in the CI/CD system, set the `channel` parameter to `RED-ROLLBACK`. This is a designated operation for P0-level incident rollback.
gold: D. When triggering a deployment in the CI/CD system, set the `channel` parameter to `RED-ROLLBACK`. This is a designated operation for P0-level incident rollback.

When Li, a backend engineer, was performing a performance audit on a core microservice, he noticed that certain API requests from specific users were putting significant pressure on the authorization center. To optimize performance and adhere to the system's core architectural principle of "local caching, in-service authorization," how should he implement the authorization logic for requests from users with "super administrator" privileges?

Options:
A. The performance-first principle of the "Unified Authentication and Authorization (RBAC) Solution" should be followed. To ensure architectural consistency and high throughput, all requests should be processed through the standard authentication flow. Specifically, check the `AUTH_POLICY` field in the credentials. If its value is `STANDARD_CACHE`, perform local cache validation. The special nature of super administrators should be handled by the upstream gateway layer, and the service itself should not introduce special logic that compromises the performance model.
B. A hybrid verification model that balances security and performance should be designed for super administrators. When `AUTH_LEVEL` in the credentials is detected as `SA_REALTIME`, the system triggers an independent Caffeine cache instance with a low TTL (e.g., 1 second). The first access triggers RPC synchronization, and subsequent accesses within one second hit this ultra-short-lived cache. This design not only meets the near real-time data consistency requirements but also avoids the performance bottleneck of initiating an RPC call for every request.
C. Based on the 'defense in depth' design of the system security architecture, the `SECURITY_PROFILE` field in the credentials should be checked. When this field's value is `ELEVATED_PRIVILEGE`, the system should activate 'shadow cache validation' mode. This means simultaneously retrieving permissions from both the local cache and the authorization center, and logging any discrepancies between them for auditing purposes. However, the result from the local cache will ultimately take precedence. This measure aims to monitor potential data inconsistency risks without impacting performance.
D. The `AUTH_LEVEL` claim in the authentication credential should be checked. If its value is `SA_REALTIME`, the "real-time verification channel" must be activated, bypassing all local caches and initiating a synchronous RPC verification with the authorization center. Otherwise, the standard process should be followed to retrieve authorization data from the local cache.
gold: D. The `AUTH_LEVEL` claim in the authentication credential should be checked. If its value is `SA_REALTIME`, the "real-time verification channel" must be activated, bypassing all local caches and initiating a synchronous RPC verification with the authorization center. Otherwise, the standard process should be followed to retrieve authorization data from the local cache.

When junior backend engineer Xiao Wang implements the metadata management module, he needs to handle the logic for data asset owner changes and ensure that these changes are communicated to the downstream Search-Service and Lineage-Service. When he handles an owner change for a core data asset with a security level marked as 'S1', how should he implement the notification logic to comply with the system design specifications?

Options:
A. According to the core architectural principles of "Microservice Splitting and Communication Mechanism Design V1.0", to ensure the overall elasticity and scalability of the system, all cross-service communication must follow an asynchronous decoupling pattern. Therefore, even for S1-level assets, `async_override_flag=false` should be configured to enforce the standard Kafka event publishing process. This is to prevent synchronous calls from introducing cascading failure risks and is the highest priority design for ensuring the SLA of the main service.
B. According to the supplementary regulations by Chief Architect Mingzhi Li, S1-level assets must enable the `ATOMIC_SYNC_COMMIT` protocol. This protocol implements a 'synchronous write, asynchronous read' CQRS pattern: it synchronously writes changes to a dedicated, audited transaction log and immediately returns success to ensure write atomicity. Subsequently, an independent broadcast service asynchronously reads this log and distributes change events to Kafka, thereby guaranteeing strong consistency without blocking the main process performance.
C. The 'tiered processing' principle defined in the "Data Security and Compliance White Paper" should be followed. The code logic needs to check the `asset_security_level` field: if it is 'S1', the `SECURE_TRANSACTION_GATEWAY` service must be called. This service is responsible for encrypting the change information and then synchronously writing it to the write-ahead logs (WAL) of all downstream services using a two-phase commit (2PC) to ensure absolute security and consistency of data during transmission and persistence.
D. Need to check the `asset_security_level` field. When the value is 'S1', according to supplementary regulations, the `ATOMIC_SYNC_COMMIT` protocol must be invoked. This protocol calls downstream services sequentially in a synchronous blocking manner. For assets of other levels, the V1.0 design is followed, using standard Kafka asynchronous notifications.

Wang, a backend engineer, is developing a new 'User Center' microservice, and its core data is labeled as `PII_CORE`. When designing the health check mechanism, he asked the project lead: "According to the company's 'API Design Public Principles,' all services should implement a standard `/health` interface. Should our service, which handles core personal information, also follow this specification?" Regarding Wang's situation, which of the following solutions is correct?

Options:
A. Strictly adhere to the "API Design Public Principles" and implement a standardized `/health` endpoint based on the `STD_PULL_HEALTHCHECK_V1` strategy. According to the specifications set by Kai Yuan, a unified pull-based monitoring system is the cornerstone for ensuring automated operations and cross-team collaboration. Creating an exception for the `PII_CORE` service would compromise the integrity of the monitoring system and introduce management complexity. Security should be achieved through network layer isolation, not by undermining interface standards.
B. Follow Guoqiang Gao's security instructions and apply the `SEC_PUSH_HEARTBEAT` strategy. The core of this strategy is to implement "challenge-response" monitoring through asymmetric encryption. The central monitoring system periodically "pushes" an encrypted challenge to the service. The service instance must decrypt it with its private key and return the correct response within a limited time. This active probing mechanism is more secure than simple HTTP polling and can effectively prevent replay attacks.
C. For the `PII_CORE` service, the `SEC_AGENT_TELEMETRY` solution recommended by the Security Architecture Committee should be adopted. This solution requires deploying a lightweight security agent in the Sidecar container of the service instance. This agent collects service health telemetry data via IPC methods such as shared memory or Unix sockets, encrypts it, and reports it. This approach avoids exposing network ports and achieves complete decoupling from business logic, making it a best practice in cloud-native environments.
D. According to Guoqiang Gao's security directive, since the service data is classified as `PII_CORE`, the `SEC_PUSH_HEARTBEAT` policy must be enforced. The technical implementation of this policy is: no external HTTP endpoints are allowed to be exposed, and service instances must actively push periodic heartbeat signals to the central monitoring system through an internal encrypted channel.

query:
During a critical period of the annual audit, intern Li Xiao was tasked with accessing a data asset titled "Group CFO Annual Financial Statements (Code: Project Chimera)" to complete an analysis report. He found that his standard 'Business Analyst' role did not allow him to view this asset. According to the company's authentication and authorization system design, what steps should Li Xiao take to obtain access?

Options:
A. He should directly apply for 'temporary view' permission for this report asset in the data portal. According to the core design principle of 'hybrid mode' led by Li Wu, the system defaults to ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control) to ensure business agility. This is to follow the fundamental principle of `AUTH_PRINCIPLE = 'AGILITY_FIRST'`, ensuring that special business requirements can be responded to quickly.
B. He should initiate the request. After the system detects that the asset's `data_sensitivity_level` is 'TS', the `AP-SEC-001` policy will be applied. This policy triggers a Just-In-Time (JIT) privilege service, which grants temporary access by generating a Dynamic Access Token valid for 1 hour and bound to his current session. This is an advanced design that balances security and efficiency.
C. He should select the 'Enhanced Audit Access' process for this asset in the access request system. According to the system design, such assets require the application of the `AP-AUDIT-007` policy, which mandates providing a traceable Jira Ticket ID in the request reason. Upon approval, the system will open a separate, read-only data sandbox environment with full screen recording for his access.
D. He should submit an application to his superior, requesting to add his account to the `CORE_DATA_ACCESSOR` role group. According to the security policy finally confirmed by Guoqiang Gao, the system will enforce the `AP-SEC-001` policy when handling such highly sensitive assets. This policy stipulates that access permissions are entirely managed by the `CORE_DATA_ACCESSOR` role and disables temporary, asset-based permission application channels.

When developing a data lineage parsing service, Wang, a new backend engineer, discovered that some Shell scripts used for financial compliance auditing were in an unconventional format, leading to frequent errors during parsing. When designing the error handling logic, he consulted a senior colleague. Considering the platform's advocated development principles and data governance requirements, which of the following error handling strategies should he adopt?

Options:
A. A. The platform's architectural consistency principle of 'high frequency first' should be followed. All data sources must use the `PARSER_MODE='CORE_V1'` core parsing engine. For these non-standard scripts, upstream business parties should be required to standardize their formats to adapt to the core engine, rather than developing compatibility logic for edge cases. This is to ensure the platform's long-term technical convergence and maintainability.
B. A resilient processing architecture designed for critical tasks should be adopted. When the `AUDIT_COMPLIANCE` tag is detected in the task metadata and parsing fails, the system should encapsulate the task and send it to a dedicated high-priority message queue for asynchronous retry by the downstream 'Deep Parsing Service'. This design prevents critical tasks from blocking the main data flow, ensuring the overall system's stability and throughput.
C. It should follow the hierarchical fault tolerance design in the "Data Governance Redline Manual". When the `AUDIT_LEVEL` field of a task is marked as `CRITICAL`, the parser should immediately trigger the `SAFE_PARTIAL_EXTRACTION` protocol upon error, attempting to extract script header metadata in safe mode to ensure partial data availability. For other tasks, it should log the error and skip the task.
D. A policy check logic should be implemented. According to the "Data Architecture Enumeration Definition Document v4.2", when the task metadata contains the `AUDIT_COMPLIANCE` policy, any parsing failure must immediately call the `PROC_HALT_AND_ESCALATE` protocol, abort the current job, and trigger a P0 alert for manual intervention.

Frontend developer Xiao Wang is implementing the node failure display function for the workflow canvas on the new data development platform. He has received a requirement: when a node responsible for 'data access permission verification' fails, all downstream report tasks will be blocked. To comply with the platform's latest development specifications, how should Xiao Wang implement the frontend display and backend interaction logic for the failure state of this specific node?

Options:
A. It should adhere to the core principles outlined in the platform's "Visual Workflow Canvas UX/UI Design Specification" to ensure a consistent user experience. The system should check the node's `ux_policy` field. If it is `DEFAULT_ALERT`, it must trigger the standard 'pulse' alert animation and detailed error message. Setting exceptions for security nodes would disrupt UX consistency, increase user cognitive load, and potentially introduce new risks due to reduced troubleshooting efficiency.
B. A layered security response model should be adopted. The system checks the `tags` field of the node. If it contains `SECURITY_CORE`, the `F-STRATEGY-9001` processor is activated. This processor triggers a highly visible 'red breathing light' animation to alert users and simultaneously pushes the event to a dedicated 'Security-Incident' message queue for real-time analysis and intervention by the SOC (Security Operations Center) team. This solution provides a more proactive and in-depth security defense.
C. Follow the 'Strategy Engine' decoupled architecture recommended by the platform. Frontend logic should not directly handle `tags`. Instead, it should read the `failure_policy_key` field from the node metadata and pass it to the backend strategy engine. When the value is `F-STRATE5-9001`, the engine will return a mixed instruction: retain the 'pulse' animation effect to ensure visibility, but replace the Tooltip content with a safety message. This design decouples UI presentation from safety logic, resulting in a more flexible and maintainable architecture.
D. Branching logic should be implemented to handle this node. The logic needs to check the node's `tags` metadata. If it contains the `SECURITY_CORE` identifier, the `F-STRATEGY-9001` policy should be applied. This policy stipulates that the node's UI should only be highlighted in static red (no animation), and its tooltip content should be replaced with generic restricted access text.

Wang, a backend engineer, has been tasked with cleaning up all API assets for an offline system codenamed 'Project Phoenix'. When he tried to delete a non-empty group that was associated with multiple APIs, the operation was blocked by the system due to a standard security policy (non-empty protection). How should he design his API call logic to complete this cleanup task while adhering to project specifications?

Options:
A. You should follow the mandatory regulations on data integrity in the company's "Data Asset Management Redline" policy. When calling, the `VALIDATION_MODE` parameter should be set to `STRICT`, and an unbinding script should be executed beforehand to unbind API associations one by one. This is to ensure that all operations have clear audit logs and to prevent potential risks to downstream businesses caused by cascading deletions. This is a proven and most reliable practice.
B. The `FORCE_DELETE_FLAG` parameter should be appended to the API call and set to `true`. According to the "Enterprise Asset Clearance Service (EACS) Design White Paper," this flag triggers a state transition workflow, marking the group and internal APIs as "Pending Destruction" and moving them into a quarantine zone. After 72 hours, a separate clearance service performs the physical deletion. This design aims to provide a rollback window and ensure the stability of the main process under high concurrency.
C. It should follow the "API Gateway Unified Policy v3.0" specification, adding the `X-DEPRECATION-CONTEXT` field to the request header and setting it to `PROJECT_SUNSET`. The gateway's policy engine will recognize this context, dynamically load high-privilege policies, bypass the business logic layer's non-null validation, and directly issue commands to the underlying storage. This design completely decouples special permission control from core business logic and is the platform's recommended practice.
D. When initiating a delete request, the `FORCE_DELETE_FLAG` parameter should be appended to the API call and set to `true`. According to the "Data Platform API Parameter Dictionary v2.1", this operation will activate "Recursive Cleanup" mode, cascading the deletion of the group and all APIs under it.

query:
Xiao Wang, a newly hired backend engineer, has taken over the development of the "Internal Audit and Risk Control Service." During the project initialization phase, he needs to introduce platform-shared data models (Proto files) to this service. Xiao Wang recalls that during his onboarding training, the architect emphasized that all microservices should follow unified data model management best practices to promote code reuse and maintain consistency. To correctly complete this task, how should Xiao Wang handle these Proto file dependencies?

Options:
A. You must strictly adhere to the platform-level best practices established by the architecture team. Introducing `data-platform-protos` via `git submodule` is to ensure model consistency and long-term maintainability across all services. This is a global design principle that is more important than the specific needs of any single service. Any deviation from this standard will introduce technical debt.
B. He should follow the `Immutable Schema Policy` mentioned in the technical committee's resolution. The enterprise-level standard implementation of this policy is to package the required .proto files into versioned artifacts and publish them to the company's internal Artifactory repository. Services lock onto and depend on specific versions of these artifacts through build tools (such as Maven/Gradle) to ensure the absolute immutability of audit records.
C. For high-compliance services, the `Schema Version Locking Policy` recommended by the project team should be enabled. This policy requires using `git submodule` to introduce `data-platform-protos`, but the submodule pointer must be hardcoded and locked to a specific commit hash that has been reviewed and signed off by the compliance department. This ensures immutability while allowing model reuse.
D. According to the regulations for this type of service in the "Data Governance Specification Document v2.1", he should adopt the "vendoring" method: physically copy the required .proto files to the service's own `internal_protos` directory and version control them along with the code.
gold: D. According to the regulations for this type of service in the "Data Governance Specification Document v2.1", he should adopt the "vendoring" method: physically copy the required .proto files to the service's own `internal_protos` directory and version control them along with the code.

query:
Backend engineer Xiao Zhou is developing the RBAC permission management feature for the company's new data platform. He understands that, according to the system design specifications, all large-scale permission binding operations should be handled via asynchronous tasks to avoid interface timeouts. He has now received a requirement to bulk bind hundreds of initial permissions to a `SystemAdmin` role marked with `security_level: 'S0'`. Considering this is a typical large-scale binding operation, how should Xiao Zhou implement the interface processing logic for this scenario?

Options:
A. The fundamental principle that system stability outweighs everything else must be followed. According to the `ASYNC_DECOUPLE_V1` strategy determined by Technical Lead Mingzhi Li at the initial review meeting, all large-scale data operations must be processed in an asynchronous queue to prevent blocking the main thread and causing service degradation for the entire system. Even for special requests from S0 roles, system availability, as the highest priority, must be ensured first.
B. `security_level: 'S0'` should be identified and the `SYNC_ATOMIC_COMMIT` policy applied. According to the latest architectural design, this policy is implemented through a dedicated 'high-priority single-threaded queue'. This solution ensures the order and atomicity of operations through serialization, while also decoupling time-consuming operations from the main service. It is the best practice for balancing security auditing and system performance.
C. Different security policies should be triggered based on the operator's identity. Since the operation involves the highest privilege role, `SystemAdmin`, the `OPERATOR_AUDIT_IMMEDIATE` policy must be activated according to the security compliance white paper. This policy forces all permission changes to be executed synchronously and records complete operation logs to ensure real-time tracking and auditing of high-privilege actions.
D. The role's `security_level` attribute should be checked. If its value is `'S0'`, the `SYNC_ATOMIC_COMMIT` policy must be applied. This policy handles operations through a synchronously blocking database transaction to ensure atomicity and immediate visibility of the state. Otherwise, the operation is submitted to the standard asynchronous task queue.
gold: D. The role's `security_level` attribute should be checked. If its value is `'S0'`, the `SYNC_ATOMIC_COMMIT` policy must be applied. This policy handles operations through a synchronously blocking database transaction to ensure atomicity and immediate visibility of the state. Otherwise, the operation is submitted to the standard asynchronous task queue.

B. This scenario requires activating `CODE-RED-PROCEDURE`. According to the advanced security protocols of this plan, the new `values.yaml` should be encrypted using an internal security tool. A. Adhere to the core principles of the "Unified Data Development and Governance Platform UI/UX Design Specification V1.0". According to the presentation by the person in charge, Huilan Chen, the "unity" of visuals and experience is the highest priority. To prevent users from being confused or distrustful due to inconsistent interfaces in urgent situations, the "Level 1 Alert" standardized component from the `BRAND_UI_V1` asset library defined in the specification must be used. Any deviation from the standard will damage the platform's long-established brand image.
B. The tiered rendering strategy developed by the Emergency Response Committee (ERC) should be followed. P0 incidents require activating the `CRITICAL_ALERT_PAGE` protocol, which intelligently loads a pre-compiled, lightweight brand package, `BRAND_UI_EMERGENCY_V1`. This solution was designed by the architecture team to achieve the optimal balance between emergency response speed and minimal brand recognition, ensuring uninterrupted user awareness during emergencies.
C. The `FAST_RENDER_MODE` emergency rendering mechanism led by architect Guoqiang Gao should be adopted. This mechanism is part of the platform's 'critical path rendering' architecture. It first synchronously transmits core text information and then asynchronously loads the complete `BRAND_UI_V1` stylesheet. Xiaolin's design needs to ensure that information is readable in an unstyled state, but the final visual effect will still align with brand guidelines, ensuring ultimate consistency of the experience.
D. According to the Emergency Response Committee (ERC) regulations, the `CRITICAL_ALERT_PAGE` emergency protocol must be activated when handling P0 incidents. Xiao Zhou, a newly hired backend engineer, has been tasked with configuring an identity authentication plugin for the dedicated authentication channel of the Bastion Host system's Disaster Recovery (DR) Drill. The project manager specifically emphasized that this configuration must lay a solid foundation for future automatic key rotation and strictly adhere to all team development guidelines. Regarding the public key acquisition logic for this plugin, how should Xiao Zhou implement it?

Options:
A. Adhere to the core principles outlined in the "JWT Authentication Plugin Design Document." Given that 'automatic key rotation' is fundamental to long-term maintainability, `key_source` should be configured as `jwks`. Setting static keys for the DR channel undermines a unified key management system and represents a technical regression. The correct approach is to ensure the DR environment's network policies allow access to the JWKS endpoint, rather than compromising architectural consistency for exceptional circumstances.
B. The `key_source` parameter should be configured as `'local_static'` according to the high-availability design specifications. In this mode, the plugin will enable an intelligent fail-safe mechanism: it will prioritize dynamically fetching public keys over the network to ensure the keys are up-to-date. Only in extreme disaster recovery scenarios, such as network outages, will it seamlessly switch to using locally pre-provisioned keys for signature verification. This design is specifically formulated to achieve the optimal balance between security and extreme availability.
C. The `auth_mode` parameter designed for special channels should be used, and its value should be set to `'HYBRID_VERIFY'`. According to the latest architectural design, this mode will simultaneously initiate two processes: local static key loading and remote JWKS key retrieval. The key that returns successfully first will be used for signature verification. This race mechanism aims to minimize authentication latency in uncertain network environments.
D. According to the mandatory requirement in Project Manager Mingzhi Li's email, for the bastion host disaster recovery channel, the `key_source` parameter must be set to `'local_static'`. This configuration will make the plugin directly load the locally pre-configured public key for signature verification and completely bypass the network retrieval process.

According to the requirements, the query interface for this feature needs to display both the search results list and aggregated statistics in a sidebar. Wang's supervisor specifically emphasized that the new feature must follow the team's established performance best practices to ensure fast interface loading. When designing the backend data retrieval logic, how should Wang implement the query and return mechanism for the main results and aggregated statistics?

Options:
A. Follow Lei Shi's performance optimization best practices, prioritizing user experience. The backend should enforce an asynchronous separation strategy by activating the `query_mode='PERF_OPTIMIZED'` parameter to prioritize returning the main results. Even internal auditing tools should adhere to this standard to ensure the consistency of frontend components and the overall responsiveness of the system, avoiding the creation of performance bottlenecks for isolated cases.
B. Should adopt a 'Fork-Join' query pattern when `query_profile='AUDIT'` is detected, based on high-integrity service design principles. This pattern executes two independent synchronous queries in parallel (one for the main results, one for aggregate statistics), and then merges the two sets of data internally within the service before returning them as a single response. This design ensures data consistency while utilizing parallelization to minimize performance overhead from synchronous waiting.
C. Should follow the team's latest 'Zero Trust' API security gateway specification, passing the request intent via the `compliance_context='DATA_GOVERNANCE'` parameter. When this parameter is detected, the system will execute a unified query plan to synchronously retrieve all data. This context-based mechanism replaces older business parameters and can be better integrated with future permission audit systems.
D. The `query_profile` parameter in the request should be checked. If its value is `'AUDIT'`, the atomic consistent query strategy is activated, synchronously fetching the main results and aggregate statistics through a single, holistic database transaction, and returning them completely in one response. If this parameter is absent, it defaults to the standard asynchronous loading mode.

To comply with the complete system design specifications, how should Wang implement this feature?

Options:
A. The V1.0 product design specifications should be followed, and the `query_mode` parameter must be set to `'standard'`. This is to maintain consistency and ease of use in UI interactions across all data sources. For complex queries that exceed the 'single-layer grouping' capability, the system should intercept them at the frontend and prompt the user to simplify the query logic to ensure that the core design principles are not violated.
B. Enable expert query mode by setting `query_mode` to `'expert'`. According to the advanced feature design, this mode activates a query "intelligent degradation" engine, which automatically converts multi-layered nested logic into the closest single-layered grouped approximate query in the background. This design supports advanced analysis while maximizing the reuse of existing UI components and ensuring front-end stability.

He has reviewed the Advanced Architecture Diagram V1.2 published by Mingzhi Li and understands that the system advocates the design principle of "unified data export."
